name: Coinbase
description: Coinbase provides distinct retail App, Advanced Trade, Business, Exchange, International Exchange, Prime, Commerce, wallet, onchain, and developer-platform products. Their APIs cover market data, accounts, portfolios, payments, addresses, trading, derivatives, transfers, withdrawals, institutional workflows, and onchain activity under different legal entities and authentication systems.
agentUseSummary: Coinbase cannot yet be connected through Relay. The generic provider name does not identify whether Relay should integrate retail accounts, Advanced Trade, Business payments, an exchange, Prime, Commerce, or CDP/onchain services. Several choices expose regulated trading or irreversible fund transfer, and Relay has no approved product, jurisdiction, account type, asset, portfolio, trading, transfer, custody, or dangerous-profile contract.

blocked.label: Connect Coinbase
blocked.description: An exact Coinbase product, jurisdiction, legal entity, account and portfolio, authentication route, and permission set must be selected first.

blocked.label: Read Coinbase data
blocked.description: Profiles, accounts, balances, portfolios, assets, addresses, transactions, orders, fills, fees, payment methods, market data, and institutional or business records remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Trade on Coinbase
blocked.description: Buying, selling, converting, placing or canceling spot, perpetual, futures, derivatives, limit, market, stop, or other orders is blocked.

blocked.label: Transfer funds or act onchain
blocked.description: Deposits, withdrawals, sends, receives, account transfers, external-address transfers, payment links, payouts, staking, signing, wallets, smart-contract actions, and onchain transactions are blocked.

blocked.label: Use private or credential-based access
blocked.description: Browser or app automation, password, session or 2FA capture, API private-key exposure, raw CLI or AgentKit, undocumented APIs, and privilege probing are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Coinbase action is enabled until the product owner selects one product and approves its jurisdiction, account, portfolio, asset, trading, transfer, custody, and dangerous-profile contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No Coinbase tools are mounted before product, jurisdiction, account, asset, credential, trading, transfer, custody, market-risk, and human-oversight controls are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: Coinbase is an umbrella for several financially and technically distinct products. Coinbase App APIs can track retail accounts and transactions, trade spot and derivatives through Advanced Trade, and transfer assets; Coinbase Business, Exchange, International Exchange, Prime, Commerce, CDP, AgentKit, and wallet or onchain products have separate customers, legal contexts, key formats, signing schemes, and capabilities. Retail authentication can use OAuth with granular scopes or customer API keys with View, Trade, Transfer and Receive permissions. OAuth account selection and portfolio restrictions further change the exact authority. Under Relay's acceptance contract an implemented provider must expose its complete chosen surface, and dangerous mode removes Relay per-action approvals. Choosing one surface for the generic label would make a product, jurisdiction, regulated-trading, custody, and irreversible-transfer commitment while misleading users of the others.
providerSetup.nextAction: The product owner, legal, compliance, security, financial-risk, consumer-protection, custody, tax, support, audit, and launch owners must select and name one Coinbase product and legal context. Freeze jurisdictions, user and account types, portfolios, assets, read actions, order and derivative types, trade and transfer authority, external addresses, payment methods, staking or onchain behavior, OAuth versus customer keys, secret custody, amount and velocity limits, price and balance checks, slippage, fees, safe approvals, dangerous-profile disclosure, 2FA and travel-rule handling, idempotency, reconciliation, tax records, audit, alerts, kill switches, and incident duties. Only then may Relay implement pinned typed wrappers for that named product.

evidence.supports: Coinbase documents separate App, Business, Exchange, International Exchange, Prime, OAuth and CDP products with different key formats, signing schemes, and authorization routes.
Coinbase App APIs programmatically track accounts and transactions, trade spot and derivatives, transfer funds, and support onchain payments.
Customer API keys separately grant View, Trade, Transfer and Receive authority, including buy and sell execution and off-platform fund movement.
OAuth scopes cover accounts, addresses, buys, sells, trades, payment methods, deposits, withdrawals, sends, requests and transfers with user-selected account access.
Advanced Trade manages accounts, portfolios, market data, fees, orders, derivatives, collateral and transfers under separate view, trade and transfer permissions.
OAuth users can restrict portfolio access, and spot order creation must bind to a granted portfolio and tradable source and target accounts.
